CLINICAL HISTORY:Large, solid prepatellar mass. Chronic.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

There is a complex fluid collection within the prepatellar soft tissues, measuring 35 x 6 x 25 mm with internal hypodensity/T2 signal as well as a thick low proton density/low T2 signal rim (measuring 4 mm in thickness). The appearance is consistent with complex prepatellar bursitis. No other discrete mass lesion identified. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

The medial meniscus shows intrasubstance degeneration of the posterior horn without discrete tear. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

Medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, and biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear. The iliotibial band is intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 13 mm, within normal limits.

There is fissuring and thinning of articular cartilage overlying the medial patellar facet. Preserved medial and lateral femorotibial articular cartilage.

Low proton density/low T2 signal lesion within the anterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle measuring 23 x 9 x 9 mm without aggressive imaging features, likely representing a bone island.

Small knee joint effusion. Regional musculature is within normal limits. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex prepatellar bursitis, with a thick walled, 56 x 6 x 25 mm collection noted in the prepatellar soft tissues.
2. Mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis.
